# 2 Samuel Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 178v–179r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_010_page_001.jpg, 2SA_010_page_002.jpg

---

**10:1** And-it-was after this, and-died [the]-king of-[the]-sons of-Ammon, and-reigned Chanun his-son in-his-place.

**10:2** And-said David, "I-will-do covenant-faithfulness [chesed] with Chanun son of-Nachash, as his-father did covenant-faithfulness [chesed] with-me." And-sent David to-comfort-him by-[the]-hand of-his-servants concerning his-father. And-came [the]-servants of-David to-[the]-land of-[the]-sons of-Ammon.

**10:3** And-said [the]-princes [sarey] of-[the]-sons of-Ammon to Chanun their-lord, "Is-David honoring your-father in-your-eyes, that he-sent to-you comforters? Is-it-not in-order-to-search the-city and-to-spy-it-out and-to-overthrow-it [that] David sent his-servants to-you?"

**10:4** And-took Chanun [the]-servants of-David and-shaved half their-beards and-cut-off their-garments in-the-middle, up-to their-buttocks [ad shitoteyhem], and-sent-them-away.

**10:5** And-they-told David, and-he-sent to-meet-them, for the-men were exceedingly ashamed [niklamim me'od]. And-said the-king, "Stay in-Yericho until your-beards grow-back [yitsmach], and-[then]-return."

**10:6** And-saw [the]-sons of-Ammon that they-had-become-odious [hiv'ishu] with-David, and-sent [the]-sons of-Ammon and-hired Aram of-Beit-Rechov and-Aram of-Tsovah, twenty thousand foot-soldiers, and [the]-king of-Ma'akhah, a-thousand men, and-Ish-Tov, twelve thousand men.

**10:7** And-heard David, and-sent Yo'av and-all the-army, the-mighty-men [gibborim].

**10:8** And-went-out [the]-sons of-Ammon and-arranged battle [at the]-entrance of-the-gate, and-Aram of-Tsovah and-Rechov and-Ish-Tov and-Ma'akhah [were] by-themselves in-the-field.

**10:9** And-saw Yo'av that the-face of-the-battle was to-him from-before and-from-behind, and-chose from-all [the]-chosen-ones of-Yisra'el, and-arranged to-meet Aram.

**10:10** And the-rest of-the-people he-gave in-[the]-hand of-Avishai his-brother, and-arranged to-meet [the]-sons of-Ammon.

**10:11** And-he-said, "If Aram is-too-strong for-me, and-you-shall-be to-me for-salvation [lishu'ah]; and-if [the]-sons of-Ammon are-too-strong for-you, and-I-will-come to-save-you [lehoshi'akha].

**10:12** Be-strong and-let-us-be-strong [nitchazaq] for-our-people and-for-[the]-cities of-our-God, and-YHWH will-do the-good [ha-tov] in-his-eyes."

**10:13** And-drew-near Yo'av and-the-people who [were]-with-him to-the-battle against-Aram, and-they-fled from-before-him.

**10:14** And-[the]-sons of-Ammon saw that Aram had-fled, and-they-fled from-before Avishai, and-came [into] the-city. And-returned Yo'av from-upon [the]-sons of-Ammon, and-came to-Yerushalayim.

**10:15** And-saw Aram that they-were-struck before Yisra'el, and-gathered-themselves together.

**10:16** And-sent Hadad'ezer and-brought-out Aram that [was]-beyond the-River [Euphrates], and-they-came [to] Chelam. And-Shovakh [the]-commander of-[the]-army of-Hadad'ezer [was] before-them.

**10:17** And-it-was-told to-David, and-gathered all Yisra'el, and-crossed the-Yarden, and-came [to] Chelam. And-arranged Aram to-meet David, and-fought with-him.

**10:18** And-fled Aram from-before Yisra'el, and-killed David of-Aram seven-hundred chariots and-forty thousand horsemen, and-Shovakh [the]-commander of-his-army he-struck, and-he-died there.

**10:19** And-saw all the-kings, [the]-servants of-Hadad'ezer, that they-were-struck before Yisra'el, and-made-peace with-Yisra'el and-served-them. And-feared Aram to-save [the]-sons of-Ammon again.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — chesed:** The same word that governed chapter 9 now opens chapter 10. David's *chesed* toward the house of Nahash parallels his *chesed* toward the house of Saul — but here, the recipient refuses it, with disastrous consequences.

**v.4 — ad shitoteyhem:** Literally "up to their buttocks/hips." The shaving of half the beard was a deliberate insult to masculine honor; the cutting of garments to expose the men was a calculated humiliation designed to shame David through his ambassadors.

**v.6 — hiv'ishu:** From the root ב-א-ש, "to stink." The idiom "they made themselves stink with David" means they had made themselves odious/detestable in David's estimation. It is the same verb used in 1 Sam 13:4.

**v.12 — nitchazaq:** The hithpael imperative "let us strengthen ourselves" is Joab's rallying cry. The theological conclusion — "YHWH will do what is good in his eyes" — is not fatalism but trust. Joab commits the outcome to YHWH after doing everything tactically possible.

**v.18 — seven hundred chariots vs. seven thousand:** The MT reads "seven hundred chariots" (שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת רֶכֶב). The parallel in 1 Chr 19:18 reads "seven thousand charioteers" (שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים רֶכֶב). Also, the MT here says "horsemen" (*parashim*) while Chronicles says "foot soldiers" (*ragliy*). The Leningrad Codex reading is preserved.

*— EMET*
